recommendations.author: Ursula K. Le Guin

recommendations.title: Pirate Cinema
recommendations.author: Cory Doctorow
recommendations.reason: Their interest in dystopian fiction examining surveillance, media, and corporate power (The Circle, V for Vendetta, Chain-Gang All-Stars, Screen People on their list) aligns well with this near-future novel about youth revolt against draconian internet censorship.

recommendations.title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
recommendations.author: Ottessa Moshfegh
recommendations.reason: Their interest in dark, psychologically intense literary fiction featuring morally uncomfortable protagonists (Lolita, The Rules of Attraction, Beautiful World Where Are You, The Guest) suggests they would be drawn to this bleak, sardonic portrait of dissociation and self-destruction.

recommendations.title: The Grip of It
recommendations.author: Jac Jemc
recommendations.reason: Their strong appetite for literary haunted-house horror that blurs psychological and supernatural dread (The Haunting of Hill House already read, The Last House on Needless Street, Hidden Pictures, The September House) makes this formally inventive, deeply unsettling debut an ideal recommendation.

recommendations.title: Something Wicked This Way Comes
recommendations.author: Ray Bradbury
recommendations.reason: Their love of atmospheric, literary horror and dark fantasy with a mythic quality (The Night Circus, It, We Have Always Lived in the Castle) makes this lyrical, deeply unsettling tale of a sinister carnival arriving in a small town a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Little Stranger
recommendations.author: Sarah Waters
recommendations.reason: Their appreciation for psychologically ambiguous, slow-burn gothic horror with literary weight (Fingersmith already on their list, The Haunting of Hill House, Dark Matter, The Comfort of Strangers) makes Waters's deeply unsettling postwar haunted-house novel an ideal next read.

recommendations.title: The Haunting of Alma Fielding
recommendations.author: Kate Summerscale
recommendations.reason: Their interest in gothic horror and the paranormal (The Haunting of Hill House, Dark Matter, Our Wives Under the Sea) combined with their taste for narrative nonfiction (Killers of the Flower Moon, The Wager) makes this true-crime investigation into 1930s poltergeist phenomena a strong fit.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Their love of gothic horror with literary ambitions (Rebecca, The Haunting of Hill House, The September House) and historical settings (Fingersmith, The Poisonwood Bible) points directly to this atmospheric, mid-century Mexican haunted-house thriller.

recommendations.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
recommendations.author: Amor Towles
recommendations.reason: Their appreciation for sprawling, character-rich literary fiction with historical depth (The Thousand Autumns of Jacob de Zoet, The Books of Jacob, Fingersmith) suggests they would love this elegant novel of a Russian count under house arrest across decades of Soviet history.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their fondness for mind-bending metafictional hybrids of horror and science fiction (House of Leaves, How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe, Piranesi) aligns perfectly with this experimental thriller about a man hunted by a conceptual shark through the fabric of narrative itself.

recommendations.title: Jonathan Strange and Mr Norrell
recommendations.author: Susanna Clarke
recommendations.reason: Their love of literary fantasy with historical grounding and dark atmosphere (The Night Circus, Fingersmith, The Monk, We Have Always Lived in the Castle) makes this sprawling, footnote-laden tale of rival English magicians in the Napoleonic era an ideal match.

recommendations.title: Ill Will
recommendations.author: Dan Chaon
recommendations.reason: Their taste for psychologically complex literary thrillers with unreliable narration and dark themes (Gone Girl, House of Leaves, Night Film, The Secret History) makes this formally experimental novel about a psychologist whose past conviction unravels alongside a possible serial killer case a compelling choice.

recommendations.title: Tigana
recommendations.author: Guy Gavriel Kay
recommendations.reason: Their taste for richly layered literary fantasy with historical texture and emotional weight (The Books of Jacob, The Thousand Autumns of Jacob de Zoet, The Way of Kings, The House of the Spirits) makes this sweeping novel about a conquered land whose very name has been erased from memory a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Beautiful Thing That Awaits Us All
recommendations.author: Laird Barron
recommendations.reason: Their overlap of literary horror, weird fiction, and psychological darkness (The Only Good Indians, What Moves the Dead, Our Wives Under the Sea, Dark Matter) suggests they would appreciate this collection of cosmically menacing, beautifully written horror stories steeped in Pacific Northwest dread.

recommendations.title: The Secret House of Death
recommendations.author: Ruth Rendell
recommendations.reason: Given their interest in psychological thrillers like The Comfort of Strangers and the works of Tana French, Rendell's taut, character-driven suspense would be a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Book of the New Sun
recommendations.author: Gene Wolfe
recommendations.reason: Their fondness for ambitious, literary speculative fiction like Hyperion, Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, and The Way of Kings suggests they would appreciate this densely layered, unreliable-narrator far-future epic.

recommendations.title: Maniac Magee
